Annotation.String: This property shall represent the NVIDIA OEM properties for a LogEntry resource.
This property shall represent the NVIDIA OEM properties for a LogEntry resource.
The section type of the event.
This property shall contain the section type to indicate the CPER event class.
The FRU ID in UUID format.

This property shall contain the Field Replaceable Unit(FRU) ID in Universally Unique Identifier(UUID) format for the CPER event. RFC4122 describes methods to use to create the value. The value should be considered to be opaque. Client software should only treat the overall value as a universally unique identifier and should not interpret any sub-fields within the UUID.
The severity of the CPER event.

This property shall contain the severity of the condition that created the CPER event. Services can replace the value defined in the ACPI or the message registry with a value more applicable to the implementation.
The IP signature.
This property shall contain the IP signature to identify the IP for common vendor specific records.
The ACPI severity of the CPER event.

This property shall contain the ACPI-defined severity of the condition that created the CPER event. Services can replace the value defined in the ACPI with a value more applicable to the implementation.
The socket number.
This property shall contain the socket number to indicate where the error occurred.
The vendor ID of this PCIe function.
This property shall contain the PCIe vendor ID of the PCIe device function.
The device ID of this PCIe function.
This property shall contain the PCIe device ID of the PCIe device function.
The class code of this PCIe function.
This property shall contain the PCIe class code of the PCIe device function.
The PCIe function number.
This property shall contain the PCIe function number within a given PCIe device.
The PCIe device number.
This property shall contain the PCIe device number within a given PCIe device.
The PCIe segment number.
The PCIe segment number is used to distinguish segments in the topology of the PCIe bus.
The PCIe device bus number.
The PCIe device bus number is a numeric identifier assigned to individual devices within the PCIe bus for effective differentiation and management.
The PCIe secondary bus number.
The PCIe secondary bus number is an identifier assigned to distinguish secondary buses in the PCIe architecture.
The PCIe slot number.
The PCIe slot number is a unique identifier for efficient recognition and management of connected devices.
The name of the device that caused this log entry.
This property shall contain the name of the device the error occurred on.
The Error ID of the event from the Error Catalog.
This property shall contain the Error ID, an identifier from the Error Catalog that identifies the specific error that occurred.
CPU In-System Test.
The In-System Test (IST) is idle.
Verifying In-System Test (IST) collateral.
Pending In-System Test (IST) boot.
Pending power cycle.
Running In-System Test (IST).
In-System Test (IST) cleanup.
One or more In-System Test (IST) tests failed.
The In-System Test (IST) run was aborted before completion.
An unexpected error occurred during the In-System Test (IST) run.
Additional data for In-System Test (IST) events in log entries.
This property shall contain IST-specific properties for a log entry that is associated with an In-System Test (IST) event.
The type of In-System Test (IST) that was performed.
This property shall contain the type of In-System Test (IST) that generated this event.
The current or final In-System Test (IST) execution stage.
This property shall contain the IST execution stage at the time this event was generated.
The In-System Test (IST) progress percentage.
This property shall contain the IST progress as a percentage from 0 to 100 at the time this event was generated.
The overall In-System Test (IST) result.
This property shall contain the overall result of the IST run at the time this event was generated.
The comma-separated list of requested test numbers.
This property shall contain the comma-separated list of specific test numbers that were requested for this In-System Test (IST) run. If not provided, all tests were run.
The comma-separated list of packages that were tested.
This property shall contain the comma-separated list of package identifiers that were tested during this In-System Test (IST) run.
An indication of whether the In-System Test (IST) was configured to continue on failure.
This property shall indicate whether the IST run was configured to continue testing after encountering a failure.
A human-readable message providing additional details about the In-System Test (IST) error or status.
This property shall contain a human-readable message that provides additional context or details about the IST result, such as a description of the failure encountered.
In-System Test (IST) details for this log entry.
This property shall contain the IST-specific details when this log entry is associated with an In-System Test (IST) event. This property shall only be present for IST-related platform events.
BIOS POST code details decoded from a platform error log entry.
This property shall contain the decoded BIOS POST code fields for a log entry that is associated with a pre-UEFI platform error.
The raw BIOS POST code value as a hex string.
This property shall contain the raw 32-bit BIOS POST code value encoded as a hexadecimal string.
The CPU socket number that reported this POST code.
This property shall contain the CPU socket number identifying which processor package reported this BIOS POST code.
The firmware stage that reported this POST code.
This property shall contain the name of the firmware stage (e.g., PSCROM, PSCFMC, MB1) that generated this BIOS POST code.
The firmware instance number.
This property shall contain the instance field extracted from the BIOS POST code, identifying the specific sub-component or context within the reporting firmware stage.
The operation code from the POST code.
This property shall contain the opcode field extracted from the BIOS POST code, identifying the specific operation that was in progress when the error occurred.
BIOS POST code details for this log entry.

This property shall contain the decoded BIOS POST code details when this log entry is associated with a pre-UEFI platform error. This property shall only be present for BIOS POST code platform error events.
